kjv: Ye shall buy meat of them
mine: You shall buy food from them
note: Hebrew 'okhel is food in general; "meat" now means animal flesh only (also v.28).

mine: they too are counted as Rephaim
note: Hebrew repha'im is the name of an ancient population group (cf. Gen 14:5), here a category the Emim belong to; the KJV translates it as "giants", turning an ethnic name into a description.
Hebrew has no verb of saying; in context the command continues Yahweh's speech (cf. v.24), but the KJV supplies "said I", making Moses the speaker.

kjv: a land of giants: giants dwelt therein
mine: a land of Rephaim. Rephaim formerly lived there
note: Again repha'im, a people name (Ammonite "Zamzummim"), rendered "giants" by the KJV.
Hebrew chatserim is the common noun "unwalled settlements, villages"; the KJV treats it as a place name.
